messages:
maya: heads-up — ORD egress observed sustained packet loss to inter-region gateways for ~18m, GPU pods showing increased queue length and prefix-kv miss spikes. starting a light traffic escape now :warning:
ryan: copy. are we seeing this from a single AZ or the whole region?
jules: metrics look like two AZs with upstream route flap. provider says partial BGP withdraw in ORD-west. not a full region outage but egress path is intermittent.
kim: starting weighted route shift to reduce ORD egress percentage to 25% and route remainder to AMS/SFO. will use canary flows first.
maya: do not shift more than 50% until we validate KV cache warmup. keep canary at 5% across 3 minutes then step.
ryan: running canary now with route override: ```json
{"route_weights": {"ord": 0.25, "ams": 0.5, "sfo": 0.25}, "canary_pct": 5, "canary_duration_s": 180}```
ops-bot: deploy-notice: traffic-escape-overlay applied by kim.
jules: observed latency increase on AMS for first minute but token error rate stable. cache misses spike but fall back after warmup.
maya: good. action items we should capture for runbook edits: 1) explicit egress flap detection (BGP withdraw + prefix-loss > 5% sustained 10m) 2) automated canary sequencing instead of manual step 3) preflight check for reserve burst capacity and billing guardrail check 4) network contact template for provider escalation. putting owners.
ryan: also add a step to temporarily prefer cached-KV model variants during egress degradations (lower cross-region bandwidth). reduces token cost and failures.
kim: noted. will draft PR to the runbook. linking current playbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/egress-escape (draft)
maya: for Dedicated customers we should add a decision matrix: when to honor reserved pool vs shift traffic (cost vs SLO). right now it's ambiguous.
jules: agree — propose a small lookup table with committed capacity tiers and recommended maximum shift rate.
ops-bot: alert: quota-check passed for burst-queue increase. cost-estimate for this shift ~+$420/day if sustained.
ryan: add automated cooldown: once ORD seen stable for 15m with <1% packet loss, bring weights back in 3 steps over 10 minutes. record rollback hysteresis.
kim: drafting playbook PR with edits: detection rules, canary automation pseudo-code, cooldown timings, cost guardrail snippet. pinging owners: @maya, @ryan, @jules for review.
maya: assign owners and deadlines: runbook PR by EOD tomorrow (kim), canary automation ticket (infra) by Friday (ryan), reserved-pool decision doc (product+finance) next week (maya).
jules: follow-up: add synthetic egress probes per AZ to detect upstream routing issues earlier. small infra task.
ryan: also add instrumentation: show per-region KV-warmup time and add alert when warmup > expected percentile.
maya: thanks all. postmortem note: root cause upstream BGP withdraw; mitigation effective. primary outcome = new detection + automated canary + decision table for reserved capacity. I'll open the retro doc and attach runbook PR link. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: incident-log: ORD-egress-degen created, severity: P2, owner: maya.
sre-bot: reminder: add test case to chaos harness to simulate partial egress withdraw and validate canary automation once implemented.
kim: PR link will be posted in the thread once ready. closing operational loop after PR review. :thumbsup:
summary: ORD region egress packet loss caused GPU queueing; team performed weighted route escape, validated KV warmup, and decided on runbook updates: egress detection rules, automated canaries, cooldown timings, reserve capacity decision matrix, and added instrumentation and synthetic probes. owners and deadlines assigned.
